( Why a website )

People check you online before they ever walk in.

Before a new customer visits, calls, or books, they search. What they find in those ten seconds decides whether you get the visit or your competitor does.

If the site is slow, unclear, or missing, they leave.

No hours. No menu. No phone number where they can find it. Most visitors will not dig for any of it. They just tap the next result.

A site that answers fast brings in customers.

Clear pages, honest details, and one obvious next step. That is what I build: a website that works like your best front desk, day and night.

( Services )

What I can
build for you

The look and layout of your site, designed around what your customers need to find: hours, menu or services, prices where you want them, and how to reach you. You see the direction on real pages early, and where it helps I build two directions to choose between, like the two Nanee versions above.
I build the full site and put it live: every page, checked on phone and desktop before it is called finished. Fast loading, clear structure, and easy to add new pages or work to later as your business grows.
Founding clients: $500 for a complete business website. No hourly meter and no surprise add-ons. Email me what your business does, and I will reply with honest next steps, including whether I am the right person for it.

A good website is not decoration. It is the hardest working page your business has.

( Questions )

Before you
hire me

The questions local business owners actually ask before having a site built. Anything else, just email me.

My first founding clients get a complete business website for $500, with the price agreed in writing before any work starts. No hourly meter and no surprise add-ons. After the founding spots are filled, I quote each project in writing first.

It depends on the size of the site and how quickly you can send me your details, like your menu, hours, and photos. I will give you a clear timeline in writing before we start, and you see the design direction early, on real pages, not at the very end.

One email is enough. Tell me what your business does, who it is for, and any site you like the look of. From there I will ask for the basics: your hours, your services or menu, your contact details, and any photos you want used.

Yes. Most of your customers will find you on a phone, so I build phone first and check every page on both phone and desktop before calling it finished. Hours, menu, and your phone number stay easy to reach on a small screen.

Yes. Sites are built so new pages and new work can be added later, the same way each new client site gets added to this page. If your hours, menu, or services change, email me and we will get it updated.

I am Addison Felizola, a Mechanical Engineering student at the University of Washington Tacoma. The honest answer is on this page: four live sites you can open and judge in about ten seconds each. That work, not a pitch, is why to hire me.

( About )

Designed and built by one person, start to finish.

I am Addison Felizola. I build websites for businesses, and I am based in Tacoma, Washington.

I also study Mechanical Engineering at UW Tacoma. That training shows up in the website work: I care about how things are put together, I check the details, and I do not call a thing finished until it has been tested the way a visitor will actually use it.

The four sites above are the proof. Two are client projects, one is a second design for the hotel, and one is a sample site. Every one is live and can be opened and judged in about ten seconds.
